topic: The Pi Collision Mystery: Why Colliding Blocks Compute Pi
target_audience: Undergraduate Physics/Math students and advanced High School students

sections.title: The Impossible Experiment
lecture_lines: Two blocks and a wall on a frictionless surface.
Large block mass is a power of 100.
Total collisions reveal the digits of Pi.
animations: Show a frictionless floor #333333 and a vertical wall [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg] #FFFFFF.
Small block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] #0000FF and massive block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] #00FF00 appear.
Massive block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] #00FF00 slides left toward the small block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg].

Animate blocks [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] colliding and small block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] bouncing off wall [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg].
A counter #FFFF00 increments with every hit.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Laws of the Game
lecture_lines: Energy and momentum are conserved in elastic collisions.
We map block velocities to a 2D state space.
Every state is a point on a coordinate system.
animations: Display formulas for Momentum and Energy conservation in #FFFFFF.
Draw axes #888888 for velocities v1 and v2.
Place state dot #FF00FF that jumps per collision.

sections.title: The Energy Ellipse to Energy Circle
lecture_lines: Conservation of energy defines an elliptical path.
We rescale the axes based on mass ratios.
This transformation turns the ellipse into a circle.
animations: Draw a cyan ellipse #00FFFF on the velocity axes.
Highlight the ellipse #00FFFF to show mathematical complexity.
Change axis labels to v1 times sqrt(m) and v2 times sqrt(M).
Animate the ellipse #00FFFF stretching into a yellow circle #FFFF00.
Show state dot #FF00FF moving along the circle's perimeter.

sections.title: Collisions as Geometric Reflections
lecture_lines: A wall collision reflects the velocity point vertically.
Block collisions reflect the point across a tilted line.
Each collision moves the point along the circle's edge.
The path traced looks like a light beam bouncing.
Every 'clack' of blocks is a geometric reflection.
animations: Reflect state dot #FF00FF vertically across the x-axis.
Draw a slanted orange line #FFA500 and reflect dot across.
Show consecutive bounces of dot #FF00FF inside the circle.

sections.title: The Pi Connection: Arc Length and Wrapping
lecture_lines: The mass ratio determines the angle of each jump.
Massive blocks create tiny, equal angular steps.
The total path wraps around the circle's perimeter.
We are essentially counting steps to measure Pi.
Physics and geometry merge into one elegant result.
animations: Label a red arc angle theta #FF0000 on the circle.
Shrink the arc #FF0000 as mass M of the block [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg] increases.
Fill the circle's perimeter with many small reflection steps.
Display the formula N equals pi divided by theta in #FFFFFF.
Pulse the counter #FFFF00 as it reaches digits of Pi.

sections.title: Summary: The Geometry of Physics
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions are hidden geometric operations.
Pi emerges from the fundamental symmetry of energy.
A simple physical system computes nature's most famous constant.
animations: Show split-screen: colliding blocks and reflecting state dot.
Make the yellow circle #FFFF00 glow with a Pi symbol.
Fade out visuals to leave only a large Pi symbol.
